sections.content: If you have searched for 'event ticketing software' recently, you already know the problem. The top results are all built for the US, UK, or Australia. They price in USD. They connect to Stripe — which is not available in Sri Lanka. And if something goes wrong, you are calling an overseas support line that has never heard of PayHere or PickMe. Sri Lankan event organizers deserve better. This article compares every major ticketing platform available today — global and local — so you can choose the right tool for your next event.

sections.heading: What Makes a Ticketing Platform Actually Work in Sri Lanka
sections.content: Before we compare platforms, it helps to define what 'works' means in a Sri Lankan context. The stakes are different here. Your attendees pay in LKR. Your bank account is in LKR. SMS is your most reliable delivery channel — not everyone checks email consistently. And your payment gateway options are limited: PayHere is the dominant local option, while Stripe is officially not available in Sri Lanka as of 2026. Any platform that locks you out of local payment gateways is effectively not usable for most Sri Lankan organizers. Beyond payments, look at five factors: local payment gateway support, LKR pricing display, SMS ticket delivery, local customer support, and ticket delivery reliability.

sections.heading: Eventbrite: The Global Giant With Local Gaps
sections.content: Eventbrite is the most recognized name in event ticketing worldwide. It has a massive discovery marketplace, slick event pages, and strong brand recognition. For a Sri Lankan organizer, however, it has significant limitations. Eventbrite Payment Processing — its primary checkout system — is not available in Sri Lanka. This means you are limited to connecting a PayPal account or accepting offline payments. Features like reserved seating and registration transfers are unavailable without the native payment processor. On fees, Eventbrite typically charges a service fee of around 3.7% plus a fixed amount per ticket, on top of PayPal's own merchant processing fees. If your tickets are LKR 2,500, the combined fees can eat a meaningful slice of your margin. There is also no SMS delivery — Eventbrite sends email confirmations only, which can be unreliable if attendees use personal email addresses that route to spam. Eventbrite works well if you are running events aimed at an international audience or using it primarily as a discovery platform. For a local concert or corporate event in Colombo, the friction points add up quickly.

sections.heading: Ticket Tailor: Good Value, But Built Without Sri Lanka in Mind
sections.content: Ticket Tailor has earned a strong reputation among independent event organizers globally. It uses a credit-based pricing model — you pay a flat fee per ticket rather than a percentage of revenue — which can be very cost-effective at scale. Ratings consistently land at 4.8 or 4.9 out of 5 on review platforms. The platform offers solid features: tiered ticket types, custom branding, a free check-in app, and full ownership of your attendee data. The core limitation for Sri Lanka is payment processing. Ticket Tailor processes payments through Stripe, PayPal, or Square — and Stripe is not available to Sri Lankan businesses. You could route through PayPal, but this adds friction at checkout and leaves you managing currency conversion manually. There is also no SMS delivery, and no local support team. Ticket Tailor is a strong choice for organizers who already have an international setup or who are comfortable managing the payment workaround. For most Sri Lankan operations, the payment layer alone creates enough friction to rule it out.

sections.heading: Skroll: Built for Sri Lanka From the Ground Up
sections.content: Skroll is a B2B ticketing platform built specifically for Sri Lankan event organizers. It connects natively with PayHere — the dominant CBSL-approved local payment gateway — so attendees pay in LKR through a familiar, trusted checkout. Every ticket is delivered via both email and SMS immediately after purchase. There is no manual step. No waiting. No batch send at the end of the day. If email delivery fails, SMS acts as the automatic fallback. The platform supports full white-labelling — your ticket designs, checkout pages, and confirmation emails carry your branding, not Skroll's. The team is Sri Lanka-based, which means support conversations happen in the same time zone and with full awareness of local event formats, cultural requirements, and operational realities. Skroll handles events from 50-person corporate workshops to large-scale concerts and festivals. The real-time dashboard lets your team monitor sales and revenue as they happen — not the next morning from an export.

Stripe is not officially available to Sri Lankan businesses as of 2026. Any ticketing platform that relies on Stripe as its primary payment processor — without a local gateway alternative — cannot be used natively in Sri Lanka.

Choosing a ticketing platform in Sri Lanka comes down to one core question: does it actually work with your local payment infrastructure? Platforms built for Western markets create avoidable problems — from checkout friction to currency conversion to support delays. Skroll was built to eliminate every one of those problems.
